claims_word_for_word.always_attached: One simulated task, two worlds, five fresh seeds (10-14), four fixed test start sets of 1,000 starts each. In strong current the test states also lie outside the recorded currents, so the band's effect is read where states are new too.

brackets.meaning: seeds where BCA's switch was on (stalling world), off (no-stall world)
BCA minus no caution; the full-log actor minus no caution (the harm)
no-stall world: no caution minus BCA
BCA's net across worlds; its lead over the best world-blind rival; that rival's name
BCA minus the matched even pull; BCA's largest loss to no caution elsewhere
BCA's unseen-throttle gain and overshoot loss
seeds where BCA's unseen-throttle gain was positive
the same for no caution, the hand-set range limit, version 6's BCA
the textbook rule clipped to the near-80 recorded range, in points
band costs of BCA and of the hand-set range limit; B minus A; seeds where B minus A was positive
no caution's share of steps past 80%; the largest random-rows-minus-main difference on seeds 0-4 (hand-set range limit or BCA's switched ramp)
near-80 minus main setting on the same fresh seeds: BCA, range limit, no caution

claims_word_for_word.exploratory_prefix: Exploratory, seeds 0-4, designed after seeing them; not a claim:
fill_rules: Numbers are written with one decimal ("{:.1f}"), with a minus sign when negative and no plus sign; "-0.0" is written "0.0". [P] is a share of steps written as a percentage. [S], [N], [K], [K2], [M] and [s] are whole numbers.

A number that cannot be computed, because a seed failed, a phase stopped or an arm is missing, is written "not available". A mark that needs it fails. Among the claim sentences, only claim 2's "for scale" sentence and claim 4's "Always, when both settings ran" sentence can show it (the bullets on failed seeds and missing numbers below).

[R] and [arm] are written as "the always-on ramp", "the matched range limit", "the matched even pull", "the first matched random surface", "the second matched random surface", "the hand-set range limit" or "BCA's switched ramp". When two rules that cannot switch themselves off have the same net, the first in step 2's order is named: the matched range limit, the matched even pull, the first random surface, the second random surface, the always-on ramp.
[situation] is "recorded conditions", "big waves" or "big kicks". [world] is "stalling world" or "no-stall world". [phase] is the phase's plain name in the runner's phase table.

[one clause per missed mark] lists the clauses of the missed marks, joined by "; ", in this order: the net lead; keeping the gain (one clause per situation that misses, in the order recorded conditions, big waves, big kicks); beating the even pull; then one clause per failed seed, in seed order. [clauses as in claim 1] is the same for the main setting. When a seed failed, a missed mark whose number is not available because of that seed is told by the seed's own clause only.

[check] is the name of the first check that failed, in the order of section 8.1; "its [phase] phase" for a stopped phase; or "its evaluation (numbers missing)" for a seed whose evaluation lacks a number (the bullets on missing numbers below). [value] is written with four significant digits, and [threshold] as section 8.1 writes it.
[reason] in claim 1's validity sentence is the harm reason when the harm is below 30 points, the past-80 reason when the share is below 25%, and both, joined by "; ", when both fail.
In the harm stop, "[or: ...]" is left out when only the harm fails; the second form replaces the first when only the share fails; when both fail, the two forms are joined by " and ".
In the reproduction stop, the bracket lists every item that differed, written "A", "A and B" or "A, B and C".

Claims 2 and 3 are written only when claim 1's validity holds, except that in the exploratory look the dropped sentence of claim 3 is written whenever the noise floor fails. When a number the noise floor needs is missing on any of seeds 0-4, the noise floor cannot be read: claim 3 is dropped as if it had failed, and the "not measured" form of the dropped sentence is written instead, with [seeds] listing the seeds where a number is missing. When check 10 fails in more than one fresh seed, the check-10 sentence is written once, for both claims, in place of claim 2's sentence and claim 3's. The "for scale" sentence is written whenever the near-80 setting ran on the group's seeds.

When a seed failed for claims 1-3, claim 2's sentence and claim 3's "Holds" or "Fails" sentence are replaced by their "If a seed failed" sentences, with [seeds] listing the failed seeds; claim 1's sentence says why each one failed. When every seed of the group failed, their "If every seed failed" sentences are written instead, since no other seed is left to report. The check-10 sentence, claim 3's "Not valid" sentence and its dropped sentences keep their precedence. So a pooled number that is "not available" only because a seed failed is never written as a finding.

The validity conditions of section 9.1 are computed over the seeds that did not fail. A failed seed fails every mark of claims 1-3 and is told by its own clause in claim 1's sentence ("seed [s] failed [check] ..."); it never makes claim 1's validity fail. A seed with no failure or stop record whose evaluation lacks a number that the validity conditions, the marks or the sentences of claims 1-3 read fails in the same way, with [check] "its evaluation (numbers missing)": its learner failed (section 10). These numbers, all in the near-80 setting unless stated, are: in strong current in both worlds, the points of BCA's switched ramp, no caution and the five rules that cannot switch themselves off (claim 1's net lead and even pull); in the stalling world, the points of BCA's switched ramp and no caution in the other three situations (keeping the gain), and in strong current the full-log actor's points and no caution's share past 80% (the validity conditions), the unseen-throttle gain and overshoot loss of BCA's switched ramp, no caution and the hand-set range limit (claim 2 and its "for scale" sentence), the hand-set range limit's points, and the points of BCA's switched ramp and the hand-set range limit in the band cost's reference setting (claim 3 and its validity condition; the random-rows setting, or the main setting without the random-rows control). Version 6's BCA is left out: it can be missing by design and is reported for scale only. [M] leaves out a failed seed that has no check-10 record.

Claim 4 is kept apart from the near-80 settings. A seed with no failure or stop record whose main-setting evaluation lacks a number that claim 4 reads fails claim 4 in the same way, with the same [check]. These are the numbers of claim 1's three marks, in the main setting, and, when both settings ran, the hand-set range limit's points in strong current in the stalling world (the "Always, when both settings ran" sentence). A missing near-80 or random-rows number never fails claim 4, and a missing main-setting number fails claims 1-3 only when they read it (without the random-rows control).
Marks and conditions are decided on the unrounded numbers, so a sentence can show 5.0 next to a mark of at least 5 that was missed.

On seeds 0-4, the "Always attached" sentence is not written; every claim sentence (sections 14.1-14.4) starts with the exploratory prefix, and in them "fresh seeds 10-14" reads "seeds 0-4" and "fresh seeds" reads "seeds". The stop sentences of section 14.5 are written as they stand.

In the stop "A stop rule cannot be read", [what] is "the harm" (the harm or the past-80 share is missing), "the band's cost to the hand-set range limit", or both joined by " and "; [seeds] lists the seeds where a number is missing, written "2", "2 and 3" or "1, 2 and 3". Wherever a sentence says "seed [seeds]", it reads "seed 2" for one seed, and "seeds 2 and 3" or "seeds 1, 2 and 3" for more.

Exactly one stop sentence is written, the first that applies in this order: a no-training check, reproduction, a stop rule that cannot be read, too little harm, the rival unaffected. The claim-4 note follows any of the last three. Each stopped phase adds its own sentence.
claims_word_for_word.intro: The code fills in the brackets. Numbers are rounded to one decimal. Every bracket is pooled over seeds 10-14, in strong current, unless stated:

claim1.clause.even_pull.label: The clauses: item 3
claim1.clause.even_pull.text: it beat the matched even pull by [E] in strong current, below the 15 required

claim1.clause.failed_seed.label: The clauses: item 4
claim1.clause.failed_seed.text: seed [s] failed [check] and, by the pre-set rule, counts as failing every mark

claim1.clause.keeps.label: The clauses: item 2
claim1.clause.keeps.text: it lost [L] points to no caution in [situation], more than the 3 allowed

claim1.clause.net.label: The clauses: item 1
claim1.clause.net.text: its net across worlds of [NET] was [D] above the best rule that cannot switch itself off ([R]), below the 10 required

claim1.fail.label: Any mark fails:
claim1.fail.text: On fresh seeds 10-14, with every recorded command that had a throttle from 70% to 90% on any thruster left out of training, BCA's switched ramp did not meet its pre-set marks: [one clause per missed mark]. [last sentence]

claim1.invalid.label: Validity fails:
claim1.invalid.text: On fresh seeds 10-14, the near-80 setting did not produce the harm it was built to test ([reason]). It supports no conclusion about BCA either way.

claim1.last.claim4_failed.label: The last sentence, exactly one: item 2 (if claim 4 ran and did not pass)
claim1.last.claim4_failed.text: Step 2's exploratory result was not reproduced on these seeds in either setting.

claim1.last.claim4_not_run.label: The last sentence, exactly one: item 3 (if claim 4 did not run (choice 6 set to no))
claim1.last.claim4_not_run.text: Step 2's exploratory result, from the main setting on seeds 0-4, was not reproduced in this setting.

claim1.last.claim4_passed.label: The last sentence, exactly one: item 1 (if claim 4 passed)
claim1.last.claim4_passed.text: Its result in the main setting does not carry over to this one.

claim1.pass.label: All three marks pass:
claim1.pass.text: On fresh seeds 10-14, with every recorded command that had a throttle from 70% to 90% on any thruster left out of training and out of BCA's calibration rows, on top of the main test's removal of the densest 15% of commands, BCA's switched ramp met all three pre-set marks. Its switch turned caution on in [S] of 5 seeds where full throttle stalls and off in [N] of 5 where it does not. In strong current it gained [X] points over no caution where full throttle stalls (the full-log controller gained [H]) and lost [W] where full throttle helps: a net of [NET], [D] more than the best rule that cannot switch itself off ([R]). It stayed within 3 points of no caution or better in the other three situations, and beat the matched even pull by [E]. Where full throttle stalls and its switch was on, its controller is the same as the always-on ramp's, so that gain comes from where the ramp starts and from its height, not from the switch.

claim1.reason.harm.label: The reasons: string 1
claim1.reason.harm.text: the controller trained without caution lost only [H] points to the full-log controller (at least 30 needed)

claim1.reason.past80.label: The reasons: string 2
claim1.reason.past80.text: the controller trained without caution went past 80% on only [P]% of strong-current steps (at least 25% needed)

claim2.check10.label: If check 10 fails in more than one fresh seed:
claim2.check10.text: On fresh seeds 10-14, hiding the band moved the edge of the recorded data too little in [M] of 5 seeds. By the pre-set rule, this version makes no claim about the band. Its numbers are reported as description.

claim2.every_seed_failed.label: If every seed failed:
claim2.every_seed_failed.text: By the pre-set rule, claim 2 fails because seed [seeds] failed (claim 1 says why).

claim2.fail_fail.label: gain mark fail, overshoot mark fail
claim2.fail_fail.text: BCA's controller did not gain reliably from throttles it never saw ([G], positive in [K2] of 5 seeds; at least 5 points and 4 of 5 seeds needed) and went past 80% often enough that holding it to 80% would have added [O] (at most 5 allowed). Its caution did not stop it at the stall.

claim2.fail_pass.label: gain mark fail, overshoot mark pass
claim2.fail_pass.text: BCA's controller did not gain reliably from throttles it never saw ([G] points in strong current over the same controller held to 70%, positive in [K2] of 5 seeds; at least 5 points and 4 of 5 seeds needed).

claim2.failed_seed.label: If a seed failed:
claim2.failed_seed.text: By the pre-set rule, claim 2 fails because seed [seeds] failed (claim 1 says why); the numbers of the other seeds are reported as description only.

claim2.pass_fail.label: gain mark pass, overshoot mark fail
claim2.pass_fail.text: BCA's controller earned [G] points in strong current from throttles from 70% to 80% that it never saw, but it went past 80% often enough that holding it to 80% would have added [O] (at most 5 allowed). Its caution did not stop it at the stall.

claim2.pass_pass.label: gain mark pass, overshoot mark pass
claim2.pass_pass.text: BCA's controller used throttles from 70% to 80% that it never saw in training, to good effect: they earned [G] points in strong current over the same controller held to 70%, and holding it to 80% would have added only [O].

claim2.scale.label: Always added, for scale:
claim2.scale.text: For scale, in strong current: the stall-aware controller gains 29.3 points from the same throttles. The controller trained without caution gained [G0] and lost [O0] past 80%. The hand-set range limit gained [GZ] and lost [OZ]. Version 6's BCA gained [GV] and lost [OV]. A rule that only stays inside the recorded data scores [Q] points, against 100 for the stall-aware controller.

claim3.dropped.label: Dropped on seeds 0-4:
claim3.dropped.text: The comparison of the band's costs was dropped before the fresh seeds, because removing the same number of rows at random moved [arm]'s points by [V] on seeds 0-4 (at most 5 allowed). Its numbers are reported as description.

claim3.dropped_unmeasured.label: Dropped on seeds 0-4, not measured:
claim3.dropped_unmeasured.text: The comparison of the band's costs was dropped before the fresh seeds, because on seeds 0-4 the noise floor (how far removing the same number of rows at random moves the points) could not be measured: a number it needs is missing on seed [seeds]. Its numbers are reported as description.

claim3.every_seed_failed.label: If every seed failed:
claim3.every_seed_failed.text: By the pre-set rule, claim 3 fails because seed [seeds] failed (claim 1 says why).

claim3.failed_seed.label: If a seed failed:
claim3.failed_seed.text: By the pre-set rule, claim 3 fails because seed [seeds] failed (claim 1 says why); the numbers of the other seeds are reported as description only.

claim3.fails.label: Fails:
claim3.fails.text: Against removing the same number of random rows, drawn from calm and hard water in the same numbers, hiding the band cost BCA's switched ramp [A] points and the hand-set range limit [B] points in strong current. The pre-set advantage of 5 points in at least 4 of 5 seeds was not shown (difference [C], in [K] of 5 seeds).

claim3.holds.label: Holds:
claim3.holds.text: Against removing the same number of random rows, drawn from calm and hard water in the same numbers, hiding the band cost BCA's switched ramp [A] points and the hand-set range limit [B] points in strong current. The ramp lost [C] points less, in [K] of 5 seeds (at least 5 points and 4 of 5 seeds were required). Where full throttle stalls, this compares two shapes of caution that cannot switch off: a ramp from the data's edge (at BCA's height) and a hard limit at it.

claim3.invalid.label: Not valid on seeds 10-14:
claim3.invalid.text: On fresh seeds 10-14, hiding the band cost the hand-set range limit only [B] points against random rows (at least 5 needed). By the pre-set rule, this version makes no claim about the band's cost. Its numbers are reported as description.

claim4.both_settings.label: Always, when both settings ran:
claim4.both_settings.text: Hiding the band changed strong-current points where full throttle stalls, against the main setting on the same fresh seeds: BCA's switched ramp by [dB], the hand-set range limit by [dR], the controller trained without caution by [d0].

claim4.fails.label: Fails:
claim4.fails.text: On fresh seeds 10-14, in the main setting, step 2's result did not hold: [clauses as in claim 1].

claim4.holds.label: Holds:
claim4.holds.text: On fresh seeds 10-14, in the main setting (only the densest 15% of commands removed), step 2's result held: BCA's switched ramp met all three pre-set marks, with a net across worlds of [NET], [D] more than the best rule that cannot switch itself off ([R]).

stop.claim4_note.label: Added to any of the three stops above, when choice 6 keeps its default:
stop.claim4_note.text: This stop does not touch claim 4: the main setting ran on seeds 10-14 as planned, and its result is reported separately.

stop.harm.label: Too little harm:
stop.harm.text: Stopped before the fresh seeds: on exploratory seeds 0-4, with the band hidden, the controller trained without caution lost only [H] points in strong current to the full-log controller (at least 30 needed) [or: went past 80% on only [P]% of steps (at least 25% needed)]. There is too little harm to test. Nothing on seeds 10-14 was generated for the near-80 and random-rows settings.

stop.no_training.label: A no-training check fails on seeds 0-4:
stop.no_training.text: On seeds 0-4, before any training, the near-80 data failed [check] ([value]; needed [threshold]). The design was redrafted. Nothing was trained.

stop.phase.label: A phase stops:
stop.phase.text: Seed [s], [world]: [phase] stopped ([reason]). It was not rerun. Every mark that needs it fails.

stop.reproduction.label: Reproduction fails:
stop.reproduction.text: Stopped: with the band empty, the new code did not reproduce [the main test's removal / critic / cloned actor / no-caution actor, or step 2's plumbing-check / switched-ramp / hand-set range-limit actor] on seed 0. No result of this version stands until it does.

stop.rival.label: The rival is unaffected:
stop.rival.text: Stopped before the fresh seeds: on exploratory seeds 0-4, hiding the band cost the hand-set range limit only [B] points against random rows (at least 5 needed). The band does not change what a range limit can do, so this version adds nothing to the main test. Nothing on seeds 10-14 was generated for the near-80 and random-rows settings.

stop.unmeasured.label: A stop rule cannot be read:
stop.unmeasured.text: Stopped before the fresh seeds: on exploratory seeds 0-4, [what] could not be measured on seed [seeds], because a phase stopped or an actor's numbers are missing there. By the pre-set rule every seed is needed, so nothing on seeds 10-14 was generated for the near-80 and random-rows settings.

compute.confirmatory_seeds_10_14: about 12-16 near-80 and random rows, plus about 6-8.5 for the main setting
compute.guard: a stage that uses more than twice its forecast's upper end, or the whole run past the cap, pauses and reports; the plumbing never pauses; a pause lasts until the owner types run_near80.sh budget-continue <stage>; each typed record allows one more forecast of that stage and raises the cap by as much; no result is read differently because of a pause
compute.machine: Framework Desktop (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 16 cores), Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL with 24 GB, CPU only
compute.memory_rule: version 7's, unchanged: a phase starts only if the reserved peaks of the running phases plus its own are at most WSL's MemTotal minus 8 GiB, and MemAvailable is at least its own reservation plus 8 GiB; an unmeasured phase kind reserves 7 GiB; a measured kind 1.25 x its measured peak; policy phases max(7 GiB, 2 x measured peak). With MemTotal about 23.5 GiB, at most 2 policy phases run at once
compute.no_training_and_plumbing: about 2-2.5 (the unit tests, about 60 smoke phases and the full-length reproduction check)
compute.plumbing_peaks: the reproduction check's full-length peak serves the critic, second-critic, switch, clone, reference-actor and policy kinds; every other kind reserves the larger of 1.25 times its smoke peak and 2 GiB; either only until an official attempt of the kind is measured
compute.unit: CPU-hours (one processor busy for one hour)
compute.version6_for_comparison: estimated at 72-92 process-hours (prereg_v7.json: an estimate that stops nothing)
compute.wall_time: about 10-13 hours in three sittings (at most 2 policy phases at once under version 7's memory rule; about 12-16 CPU-hours of policy phases)
